headline: AI 的账本比模型更危险：美国科技巨头隐性 AI 债务半年膨胀 90% 至 3.2 万亿美元，而 OpenAI 被指悄悄重启 Codex 对话训练——信任与杠杆同时被透支。

overview_bullets.text: 美国科技巨头的隐性 AI 债务半年内暴涨 90% 至 3.2 万亿美元，AI 资本开支正从"技术叙事"变成"资产负债表叙事"，融资结构一旦反转，冲击会先落在算力租赁与云合约上。
OpenAI 被指在用户不知情下重新开启 Codex 对话训练，叠加 GitBook 泄露事件，企业"关掉数据共享开关"的合规假设正在失效。
今日 GitHub 热榜几乎被 agent 基础设施占满（agent-desktop、claude-mem、Claude-Code-Game-Studios），竞争焦点已从模型能力转向上下文持久化与多智能体编排。
Kling 团队与多篇论文共同指向同一判断：视频生成瓶颈从渲染转向语义控制，机器人研究则从"造模型"转向"建评测场"（RoboColosseum、PrimeSim）。
HN 上"每两个网站就要证明自己是人"的抱怨冲上热榜，反爬与反 AI 的军备竞赛正在把普通用户的浏览体验当作代价。

executive_summary: 今天最清晰的信号不是某个模型变强，而是 AI 产业的成本、信任与验证成本正在同时向用户和企业转移，而开源社区正用工程化工具抢先填补这些裂缝。

editor_note.core: 今天最该记住的是 3.2 万亿美元隐性 AI 债务——它说明 AI 竞赛的约束条件已经从"能不能做出模型"变成"谁来为算力付利息"。当资本开支靠表外结构支撑，任何一次融资窗口收窄都会通过云合约迅速传导到模型公司。
editor_note.cross_signal: 债务新闻与 OpenAI 静默重启训练、GitBook 泄露三条互相印证：产业在加杠杆的同时也在加码数据攫取，企业对前沿实验室的"信任折扣"会进一步推高自建与开源替代的需求，这正是今日 GitHub 上 agent 基础设施霸榜的底层动因。
editor_note.counterintuitive: 热度最高的都是 agent 工具与视频生成，但真正稀缺的是"评测与诊断"类工作——RoboColosseum、近零 token embedding 导致训练停滞这类论文热度平平，却直接决定前面那些炫目系统能否被信任。
editor_note.risk: 最大的盲点是数据开关的"默认值风险"：用户以为关闭即安全，但设置可被静默重置，意味着所有基于"我已退出训练"的合规声明都可能是空的；同时隐性债务让 AI 公司对数据变现的动机更强，两者叠加是今年最该盯的隐患。

contradictions: OpenAI 一方面对外强调企业数据隐私与合规，另一方面被用户指称静默重新开启 Codex 对话训练，行为与承诺相悖。
社区一边热议"AI 泡沫与金融危机"，一边 GitHub 上 agent 工具热度持续攀升，资本谨慎与工程狂热同时存在。
视频生成论文宣称迈向实时与可控，但 Kling 报告自认瓶颈已从渲染转向语义控制，说明"生成质量提升"与"可控性达标"并非同一件事。
underrated: Near-Zero Token Embeddings Silently Stall Training in Gated Sequence Models：52.6% 的非绑定门控检查点存在近零输入嵌入，是开源权重质量的系统性隐患
SpecPilot：质疑并行投机解码的"stock 系统"是否真达到理论加速，属于少见的自我拆台式系统研究
Diagnosing the Reference Gap：把多模态推理失败归因于指代而非感知，纠正了主流归因偏差
JustVugg/colibri：用 C 写的分层 MoE 推理引擎，把冷专家放 NVMe，是消费级硬件跑前沿模型的务实路线
p-e-w/heretic：免训练去除审查与谄媚，涉及对齐可逆性的敏感但重要议题

sections.name: 开源项目
sections.summary: Agent 基础设施与推理/爬虫工具占据热榜，社区在用工程手段解决上下文、成本与本地推理问题。

sections.name: 论文与研究
sections.summary: 视频生成走向智能体化与实时化，机器人研究转向规模化评测与开源 harness，同时出现对训练隐性故障的硬核诊断。

sections.name: 社区舆论
sections.summary: 数据训练默认开启、验证码泛滥与 AI 泡沫论构成今日社区三大焦虑点。

sections.name: 产业与新闻
sections.summary: 隐性 AI 债务的膨胀把产业风险从技术层推到金融层。

comments.one_liner: vercel-labs 推出的面向 AI agent 的 computer use 命令行工具
comments.why: 把「操作电脑」这一层抽象成 CLI，代理就能脱离浏览器沙箱直接驱动桌面应用，自动化边界从网页扩展到本地软件栈。
comments.stance: 方向对，但让代理拿到桌面控制权，权限与审计问题会被推到每个使用者头上。

comments.one_liner: Scrapling 是一个 Python 网页抓取框架，覆盖从单次请求到大规模爬取的全流程。
comments.why: 把单请求抓取到全站爬取的适配层收进一个框架，降低了中小团队自建采集管线的门槛，也让反爬对抗从自研转向依赖社区维护。
comments.stance: 抓取框架的竞争点已从功能多少转向反封锁存活率，谁先被主流站点识别谁就出局。

comments.one_liner: pingdotgg 开源的 t3code 代码项目仓库
comments.why: 知名开源作者的新仓库冲上趋势榜，说明社区对个人品牌驱动的脚手架项目仍愿意用 star 投票，新项目冷启动的门槛被作者信誉直接抹平。
comments.stance: 个人 IP 已成为开源项目最便宜的获客渠道，代码质量反而排在第二位。

comments.one_liner: 为各类 coding agent 提供跨会话持久记忆的工具，记录会话内容并用 AI 压缩后回注到后续会话。
comments.why: 跨会话持久记忆被做成通用层并兼容 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini 等多家代理，代理的上下文从一次性消耗品变成可累积资产，切换工具的成本随之下降。
comments.stance: 记忆层会成为代理生态里最容易被锁定的一环，谁掌握压缩与注入策略谁就掌握粘性。

comments.one_liner: mattpocock 公开的 .agents 目录中的工程技能集合
comments.why: 把个人 .agents 目录里的技能直接公开，等于把「提示词工程」沉淀为可复用资产，工程师的编码习惯开始被版本化分发。
comments.stance: 有价值，但技能包高度依赖作者个人工作流，复制到别人机器上多半水土不服。

comments.one_liner: 纯 C 编写、零依赖的推理引擎，从磁盘流式加载专家权重，在本地硬件上运行前沿 MoE 模型
comments.why: 纯 C、零依赖、专家从磁盘流式加载，意味着 MoE 大模型的显存门槛被换成磁盘 IO 门槛，消费级硬件能跑起前沿规模模型。
comments.stance: 这是本轮最硬的一条：把「大模型必须上云」的前提直接拆掉。

comments.one_liner: 把 Claude Code 配置成游戏开发工作室，包含 49 个 AI agent 与 72 个工作流技能
comments.why: 用 49 个代理和 72 个技能模拟工作室层级，把单代理编码变成多代理编排，验证的是协调系统而非模型能力。
comments.stance: 噱头大于实用，代理数量堆到几十个只会放大编排开销，真正稀缺的是收敛机制。

comments.one_liner: 无需训练即可修改语言模型行为的工具，可去除审查、抑制套话与谄媚倾向
comments.why: 免训练直接改模型行为，去掉审查、抑制套话、降低谄媚，意味着对齐从训练阶段后移到部署阶段的权重编辑。
comments.stance: 技术上漂亮，但「去审查」和「去谄媚」被打包在同一把工具里，滥用成本几乎为零。

comments.one_liner: floci 是一个轻量、免费、可本地运行的 AWS 服务模拟器，作为 LocalStack 的替代方案。
comments.why: 本地模拟 AWS 服务让开发与测试摆脱真实云账号和计费，直接压缩了 CI 环境成本与凭据泄露面。
comments.stance: LocalStack 的免费边界正在被侵蚀，这类替代品的胜负取决于服务覆盖度而非轻量。

comments.one_liner: 可灵团队发布报告，总结多代视频生成模型在语义控制与多模态理解上的观察与洞见。
comments.why: 可灵把视频生成的瓶颈从像素渲染定位到语义控制，等于宣告下一轮竞争在理解层而非画质层，模型团队的资源分配会随之倾斜。
comments.stance: 厂商自述的观察报告本质是路线宣示，语义可控性才是能收费的那一层。

comments.one_liner: RoboColosseum 是一个分布式评测框架，通过统一策略服务与标准化协议在真实环境中大规模评估机器人策略。
comments.why: 跨机器人、跨环境的分布式评测把具身智能的可复现性变成基础设施问题，缺少统一评测的团队将无法证明策略泛化。
comments.stance: 具身智能现在最缺的不是新策略而是可比的考卷，这类框架早该出现。

comments.one_liner: 一篇论文，探讨视频生成与 agent 框架结合，涵盖 agentic 视频生成、世界建模与递归自我改进
comments.why: 视频生成从端到端合成转向规划加工具调用加反馈的代理式流程，多镜头一致性靠编排而非单次生成解决，世界模型同时充当可交互环境。
comments.stance: 这是视频生成真正走向可控的路径，但代理循环带来的延迟和成本会被严重低估。

comments.one_liner: MoviEdit 是一个端到端框架，用于长时长、多镜头视频编辑并保持跨镜头一致性。
comments.why: 长视频多镜头编辑要求跨场景切换保持编辑意图一致，这把视频编辑从单帧修补推向长上下文一致性工程，直接影响影视后期工作流。
comments.stance: 多镜头一致性是视频编辑真正落地的前提，做不到就只是滤镜。

comments.one_liner: 提出 uni-robot-agent 统一框架，用开源权重模型开展 robot-use agent 研究
comments.why: 用开放权重模型加统一 harness 替代专有前沿模型做机器人操作，研究门槛从 API 预算降到本地算力，可复现性随之提升。
comments.stance: 开放权重在机器人领域追平专有模型只是时间问题，这类 harness 是必要的基础设施。

comments.one_liner: 一篇综述与路线图，主张把分散在各模态社区中的 embedding 研究整合为统一的 omnimodal embeddings 方向
comments.why: 把文本、图像、音频等各模态的嵌入研究从各自为战推向统一框架，直接决定跨模态检索与推荐系统能否共享一套表征底座。
comments.stance: 方向正确，但综述加路线图最容易沦为口号，真正的检验是能否给出可复现的统一评测基准。

comments.one_liner: SpecPilot 面向投机解码，自动发现算法并优化系统，以挖掘并行草稿的加速潜力。
comments.why: 揭示并行草稿的已发布系统未吃满理论加速比，把投机解码的优化空间从算法设计转向系统实现，推理成本还有可挖的余量。
comments.stance: 论文级加速比和线上吞吐之间的落差，才是推理降本的真战场。

comments.one_liner: 提出 Wave Forcing 方法，用于流式长视频生成，目标是逼近光速级的实时生成速度
comments.why: 把流式长视频生成的两遍前向压缩到接近光速，意味着实时连续视频从演示走向可部署，算力成本结构随之改变。
comments.stance: 效率突破比画质提升更有价值，但长视频一致性若仍靠缓存修补，实时只是把问题推后。

comments.one_liner: PrimeSim 是基于大规模跨本体演示训练的动作条件多视角世界模型模拟器，用于机器人长时序推演。
comments.why: 把世界模型当模拟器用，要求动作可控、多视角一致与长时程连贯，这决定了机器人训练能否脱离真机采集，直接冲击数据成本结构。
comments.stance: 只会生成好看视频的世界模型没有价值，动作忠实度是唯一验收标准。

comments.one_liner: NorthCUA 技术报告，介绍一套通过大规模经验积累来加速 computer-use agents 的集成系统
comments.why: 用规模化执行经验把计算机操作智能体从单步动作推向完整软件工作流，决定这类智能体能否真正替代人工操作而非演示。
comments.stance: 经验飞轮是正确路径，但技术报告若只报自家基准，说服力有限。

comments.one_liner: Kairos 是开源的实时风险与欺诈决策平台，定位为 Sift、Sardine 等的替代品。
comments.why: 开源实时风控平台把反欺诈决策能力从高价 SaaS 拉到自建，缺标注数据和欺诈者快速变异这两个痛点被摆上台面，中小支付方获得替代选项。
comments.stance: 风控开源化的真正门槛是数据闭环而非模型，先解决冷启动的才活得下去。

comments.one_liner: 一本面向生成式 AI 基础的直观数学入门小书。
comments.why: 把生成式 AI 的数学基础做成直觉化读本，降低了非科班工程师理解扩散与注意力的门槛，影响的是团队内部沟通成本。
comments.stance: 数学直觉读物比又一门框架教程更有长期价值，但别指望它替代推导。

comments.one_liner: 有用户称 OpenAI 在 Codex 中悄然重新开启了用于模型训练的对话数据共享开关。
comments.why: 数据共享开关被静默重置，意味着企业此前基于关闭状态做的 IP 保护假设失效，合规与法务需要重新审计代码助手的默认配置。
comments.stance: 默认值即政策，静默改默认就是绕过用户同意，这类行为该被强制留痕。

comments.one_liner: Gitbook 用户称在提交支持工单后收到安全事件说明，但尚未见到官方客户通报或数据泄露通知
comments.why: 用户是从客服工单回复而非官方通报中得知入侵，说明披露链条已断在厂商与客户之间，下游团队无法判断凭证、文档与集成密钥是否外泄。
comments.stance: 先假定自家 GitBook 令牌与公开文档已泄露，立即轮换并追责其披露流程。

comments.one_liner: 用户抱怨浏览网页时频繁遭遇 Cloudflare 等「验证你是人类」的验证码与拦截页面
comments.why: 验证码拦截从边缘防护变成默认入口，普通阅读与抓取成本被转嫁给终端用户，开放网页的可达性由少数 CDN 厂商单方面决定。
comments.stance: 这是反爬军备竞赛对公共阅读权的征税，站点该为可读性负责而不是把门槛甩给读者。

comments.one_liner: 一篇讨论 AI 热潮可能正在酝酿新一轮金融危机的文章
comments.why: 算力投资靠债务与循环交易支撑，一旦回报周期拉长，估值回调会沿供应链传导到电力、芯片与云厂商的现金流。
comments.stance: 泡沫论调已从嘴仗进入资产负债表，宁可提前减仓 AI 基建敞口。

comments.one_liner: 报道称美国科技巨头隐藏的 AI 相关债务在半年内增长 90%，达到 3.2 万亿美元
comments.why: 表外与隐性负债半年膨胀九成，意味着 AI 军备竞赛的真实杠杆远高于财报呈现，利率稍有波动就会挤压资本开支。
comments.stance: 3.2 万亿的隐形债是这轮 AI 叙事最脆弱的一环，透明度缺失本身就是风险。

it_6dc982f8f49f00b4.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
it_6dc982f8f49f00b4.summary: Video generation has progressed from isolated clips to coherent short-form audiovisual sequences, and the bottleneck is shifting from rendering to semantic control. This report summarizes the observations and insights on multimodal understanding gained from successive generations of Kling. We argue that generation quality is the projection of multimodal understanding through the entire data--conditioning--alignment--evaluation chain, and we examine this chain module by module. Kling-MLLM, a shared multimodal foundation model that unifies image, video, audio, synchronized audio--video, and interleaved inputs, is specialized for each downstream module. Because a DiT is trained on far fewer training samples than a language model, we treat captioning as a semantic contract that maximizes description density, and extend it to reference-grounded captioning that makes reference bindings explicit. Prompt enhancement translates user intent into this caption distribution: basic PE is derived from captions of compelling videos and refined with text-level and generator-in-the-loop reinforcement learning, while agentic PE refines the story and retrieves compelling examples. We show that a reliable text encoder comes from perceptual training rather than from stronger language ability, and that candidates can be screened from text alone before end-to-end training. Reward modeling pairs a general reward model for explainable, localized critiques with a decision reward model for fast multidimensional scoring, treating perceptual bandwidth as a first-class design parameter. Finally, we review task-specific automatic evaluation, focusing on protocols that expose scoring shortcuts and help trace failures to their upstream source. We hope these lessons offer practical guidance for building the understanding stack behind controllable video generation.

it_6d122e485808aa2d.title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
it_6d122e485808aa2d.summary: General-purpose robot policies must work across robots, tasks, and environments, yet the variation that makes physical trials informative also makes them difficult to reproduce. We introduce RoboColosseum, a distributed evaluation framework that combines unified policy serving and standardized protocols across a network of locally operated robots in diverse environments. Our initial study evaluates five vision-language-action (VLA) policies and three frontier AI agents across four embodiments (SO-101, Franka, Bimanual-YAM, and G1 Humanoid). The Open Track compares models without task-specific adaptation in blinded, pairwise trials under matched local conditions. The Fine-tune Track measures how well VLA policies adapt to 20 tasks across all four embodiments when each policy receives the same 100 demonstrations per task. Across 5,699 pairwise Open Track comparisons at 124 sites, frontier agents rival specialized VLA policies, while all systems struggle to complete open-world tasks reliably. After fine-tuning, GR00T N1.7 leads on SO-101 and pi0.5 leads on Franka and Bimanual-YAM. Policy rankings show weak agreement across embodiment-specific task suites (Kendall W = 0.24). Open Track rankings poorly predict relative performance after fine-tuning, with substantial rank reversals on all three embodiments shared between tracks. Measuring partial progress reveals differences that task success alone misses. On the G1 Humanoid, no policy completes any of the five tasks, yet average progress ranges from 13.3% to 23.2% across policies. Open Track rankings stabilize as trials accumulate, and active matchmaking achieves comparable ranking agreement with substantially fewer physical trials than uniform sampling. These results show how distributed physical evaluation can reveal where robot policies generalize, how well they adapt to new tasks, and how far they progress on tasks they fail to complete.

it_04f56b52c4358763.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
it_04f56b52c4358763.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation challenges of these systems. Second, agentic world modeling, where harnesses mediate observation, control, execution, and state. We discuss hybrid designs in which game engines or agent-written programs maintain world state while video models render observations, and how agents and world models can mutually evaluate and improve one another. Third, recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video model development, distinguishing output revisions, updates to harness state, generator parameters, and evaluators, and changes to the improvement procedure itself. We identify how these improvements feed back into subsequent development. Across these directions, we analyze essential agent capabilities, including audiovisual perception, long-horizon planning, memory, code-based interaction, feedback-guided control, skill reuse, and multi-agent coordination. We conclude with challenges in autonomous video production, lifelong memory, programmable hybrid control, autonomous model development, provenance, cost accounting, and evaluation linking video quality and task performance to sustained improvements in models and harnesses.

it_85c9daa9229f7457.title: MoviEdit: Long-form Multi-Shot Video Editing Made Easy
it_85c9daa9229f7457.summary: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit, an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of data, modeling, and evaluation. To provide cross-shot supervision data at scale, we develop automatic data-generation pipelines spanning synchronized multi-view footage, real-world multi-shot videos, and generated multi-shot content, yielding 87K paired editing videos without manual annotation. Architecturally, MoviEdit employs a cascaded bidirectional-autoregressive design: a lightweight bidirectional stage first establishes a globally coherent editing draft over a spatiotemporally compressed representation, which is then autoregressively propagated and refined over the full video. We further introduce MoviEdit-Bench, a dedicated benchmark for systematic evaluation of long-form multi-shot video editing. Extensive experiments show that MoviEdit substantially outperforms existing open-source models and performs on par with industry frontier models across text-guided and image-guided editing. Visit our project page for complete results and to access the benchmark: https://multi-shot-edit.github.io/

it_2a9dfe71c25fa67e.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
it_2a9dfe71c25fa67e.summary: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.

it_c90a52c1ce6e4b92.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
it_c90a52c1ce6e4b92.summary: Embedding models underpin virtually every modern AI system, from search engines to recommendation systems. Despite shared mathematical foundations, research on embedding models remains fragmented by modality: the communities develop largely in isolation, seldom exchanging insights. We argue that this fragmentation obscures a deeper convergence. Driven by contrastive learning, Transformer architectures, and a granularity shift, embedding research across modalities is converging toward a common set of principles, even as modality-specific challenges remain underexplored. To reason across this convergence without conflating it, we propose a framework of three progressively harder capabilities: coverage, comparability, and compositionality. Three paths toward unification satisfy these in turn: transformation broadens coverage, alignment enables comparability, and joint embedding, the terminus we advocate, aims at compositionality. This position paper traces the resulting evolution, providing the first unified, cross-cutting treatment of omnimodal embedding research.

it_c9f75cc384201fb8.title: SpecPilot: Autonomous Algorithm Discovery and Systems Optimization for Speculative Decoding
it_c9f75cc384201fb8.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates memory-bound LLM decoding with a lightweight drafter, and parallel drafters extend this speedup by drafting a whole block in one forward pass. However, it remains unclear whether their released systems (stock) attain the full speedup that parallel drafting permits. We identify three challenges. First, with one request, each step accepts few tokens but reads every target weight. Second, with batching, per-request verification work roughly halves the speedup over autoregressive (AR) decoding. Third, speculative decoding is deployment-specific, and no universal optimization fits every serving regime, drafter, target model and GPU. To address these challenges, we present SpecPilot, an autonomous agentic loop that discovers algorithms and systems optimizations for each deployment. In each round, a cost model locates the largest gaps between the current system and its ceiling. Parallel agents explore directions and integrate the successful ones. Token forcing checks every output token against stock to detect reward hacking. A structured memory carries validated mechanisms to new rounds and deployments. SpecPilot discovered a general lossless 12-bit weight format, tree verification for hybrid recurrent targets, two-level verification and three batching mechanisms. We evaluate it across four target models, three drafters, two GPU platforms and five benchmarks. Without training or quality loss, it raises the speedup over AR from stock's 4.46times to 10.87times with one request, and from 1.94times to 3.93times with batching.

it_42da0213eeb6fa65.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
it_42da0213eeb6fa65.summary: Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. We propose Wave Forcing (WF), which co-designs generation, training, and execution for continuous video output with multi-step denoising. WF uses chunk-wise causal attention to access earlier, cleaner chunks before their denoising is complete, and distributes staggered denoising and cache-refresh stages across full-model replicas to achieve 1F1C: one output chunk per concurrent forward round after pipeline fill. To adapt the model to this continuous generation process, we develop a three-stage training procedure that successively introduces mixed-noise denoising, motion supervision, and causal adaptation using self-generated history. To execute this process efficiently, Wave Runtime (WaveRT) uses Wave Parallelism (WP) for early K/V delivery and communication-computation overlap, together with optimized kernels and pipelined VAE decoding. Experiments on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B show that 5-step WF maintains overall quality comparable to Rolling Forcing while achieving higher Dynamic Degree on both short and long videos. Our system efficiency experiments show that 4-step WF achieves 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS on eight H200 GPUs, yielding 7.07x the single-GPU end-to-end throughput. In DiT-only tests with matched SageAttention+W8A8 backends, denoising steps, and GPU counts, WP delivers up to 2.53x the throughput of the faster of the Ulysses and Ring context-parallel baselines across six model scales (1.3B-14B).

it_1ab85ca2a17abe0c.title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations
it_1ab85ca2a17abe0c.summary: A robot world model that serves as a simulator must do more than generate plausible videos: it must faithfully follow commanded actions, maintain consistency across camera views, and sustain coherent long-horizon rollouts. We present PrimeSim, an action-conditioned, multiview world model simulator that addresses these challenges through progressive midtraining and posttraining. Starting from a pretrained video generator, we midtrain on 30,110 hours of robot demonstrations spanning 22 platforms. To improve action following, we introduce a unified cross-embodiment action representation and frame-aligned dual-path conditioning to strengthen action-frame correspondence. To maintain multiview consistency, we develop view-aware interleaved attention with explicit camera identities, enabling cross-view information exchange while preserving view-specific representations. We further introduce a fast-video, slow-memory posttraining framework that transforms the bidirectional video generator into an efficient autoregressive simulator. By combining fast causal generation, self-rollout training, and hierarchical temporal memory, PrimeSim mitigates error accumulation from self-generated histories and supports coherent long-horizon simulation. PrimeSim runs at 10.1 FPS, remains stable over long-horizon rollouts on rigid and deformable manipulation tasks, and transfers to held-out platforms within 100 to 200 gradient steps where the pretrained backbone does not. Against five open-source action-conditioned world models it leads four of the five WorldSimProbe suites and posts the best overall EWMBench score, while fine-grained local calibration still trails the field; its rollouts are faithful enough to support GRPO-based policy optimization. We release the model weights, inference code, and training code.

it_f954b07c153995ae.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
it_f954b07c153995ae.summary: Scaling computer-use agents from individual actions to complex software work requires experience that connects decisions to complete outcomes. We present NorthCUA, an integrated system for turbocharging computer-use agents through experience at scale. Its Experience Flywheel supplies diverse executable tasks to the NorthCUA Harness, which sustains long interactions, records decisions, and checks task outcomes. The Flywheel uses these records to curate verified trajectories. For unsolved tasks, recursive self-improvement evolves reusable skills and preserves verified milestones so later attempts build on earlier progress. Staged Learning combines this experience with grounding data from the Flywheel to develop GUI competence through mid-training and long-horizon supervised fine-tuning. The policy then learns from fresh attempts in the same Harness through joint desktop-web reinforcement learning, closing the loop between experience production and policy improvement. The resulting Nano, Mini, and Pro family achieves state-of-the-art results among open-source models across GUI grounding, desktop execution, and Web interaction under the reported evaluation settings. For more responsive Web workflows, NorthCUA-Ultrafast pairs direct action selection with open-ended generation on pre-RL Nano, offering a measured quality-latency tradeoff. Together, these advances establish NorthCUA as a high-performing model family and a reusable foundation for agents that carry complex software work from intent to completion.

it_9d9d4b889e1f4705.title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
it_9d9d4b889e1f4705.summary: Foundation models in changing environments can encounter unfamiliar domain knowledge that their original training did not cover. However, new domains rarely provide large amounts of expert-created training data or reliable supervisory signals for further training. We introduce Recursa, a foundation model system that adapts to new domains by learning from its own experience without human experts or a stronger teacher model. Recursa uses a knowledge repository to store what it learns: domain-specific skills and instructions on when to apply them, along with memories of past task experiences and reflections on what to improve. Recursa bootstraps the repository from domain materials and then refines it through recursive self-improvement. It uses parallel learners to execute tasks and synthesize local improvements, then validates and merges the improvements into the knowledge repository. On Harvey LAB's Firm Knowledge benchmark, Recursa raises the all-pass rate on held-out test tasks from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash.

it_5a9d8ef122652eaf.title: Near-Zero Token Embeddings Silently Stall Training in Gated Sequence Models
it_5a9d8ef122652eaf.summary: Among 291 surveyed open-weight language model repositories (280 distinct embedding tables), 52.6% of untied gated and hybrid checkpoints (20/38) contain reachable input embeddings with norms below 10^{-6}, compared with 0% of weight-tied models. Such near-zero rows can arise during pretraining when unseen rare or template tokens receive zero input gradients while AdamW weight decay shrinks untied embeddings. In tested Transformer configurations, non-initial positions or a BOS token prevent this failure mode. In gated sequence models (Mamba, Gated DeltaNet, xLSTM), a near-zero token can amplify input-embedding gradients by more than 30 orders of magnitude (up to 35). At zero input, current-token readout factors (SiLU gates or linear queries) vanish, suppressing historical-state readout. Residual RMS values can then fall below the square root of the RMSNorm floor across consecutive layers, causing Pre-RMSNorm to amplify backward gradients by up to 10^3 per layer. When a gradient entry exceeds 1.84 times 10^{19}, FP32 global-norm clipping in PyTorch, Hugging Face Trainer, and FSDP2 can overflow to infinity and zero the current batch's gradients. In Telugu continual pretraining of Nemotron-3-Nano-4B, this discards updates on approximately 20% of steps and leaves triggered rows frozen. We propose two remedies. For released checkpoints, GroupClip decouples input-embedding clipping using a 64-bit or rescaled norm; its rescaled implementation eliminates update loss and heals triggered rows in one step with negligible measured end-to-end overhead. For pretraining, GateFloor (SiLU(z) + δ, δin [0.01, 0.1]) keeps the gate positive at zero input, reducing near-zero gradients by 28 orders of magnitude in experiments up to 370M parameters, with perplexity comparable to the baseline.

it_420c7409c05b7e7d.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning
it_420c7409c05b7e7d.summary: Multimodal large language models can recognize visual content yet struggle to reason reliably over it across multiple steps. In counting, a model may see all objects but lose track of which ones it has counted. We argue that such failures, commonly attributed to perception, reveal a reference gap: the failure to bind language to the relevant visual entities, regions, or locations. Motivated by the theory of visual routines, we test whether external references such as numbering can narrow this gap. We introduce ReGap-Bench, a paired benchmark of five visual reasoning tasks in which the scene, question, and answer are fixed and only the reference varies. Results show that task-matched references improve accuracy by up to 25\%, while mismatched references provide little benefit or even hurt performance. These findings identify the reference gap as a bottleneck distinct from visual perception and show that constructing task-appropriate visual references can serve as a training-free visual skill for improving multimodal reasoning.

it_a5996ff76c418a8c.title: ParetoSaddler: Pareto-Guided Optimization of Agent Harnesses for Quality and Cost
it_a5996ff76c418a8c.summary: Harness optimization can substantially improve LLM agents without modifying model weights, but existing methods primarily optimize response quality. Extending them to joint quality--cost optimization introduces a challenge: applying the deployment preference during intermediate updates can prematurely reject candidates that are valuable for later improvements. We introduce ParetoSaddler, which addresses this mismatch by separating intermediate candidate promotion from final deployment selection. At each iteration, an optimizer updates a parent harness to produce a candidate, and then compares the two over repeated executions and uses Bayesian bootstrap Pareto support to promote candidates showing credible progress in either quality or cost. Promoted candidates receive broader development evaluation and remain available as parents for later optimization steps. We evaluate ParetoSaddler on ClawMark and GAIA2 using domain-disjoint splits. On ClawMark, ParetoSaddler improves quality from 70.86\% to 81.35\% while reducing cost from \1.17 to 1.01 per task; on GAIA2, it improves quality from 56.22\% to 62.89\% while reducing cost from \0.78 to 0.45 per task. The Pareto-selected harnesses also achieve higher quality at lower cost than quality-only harness optimization. Analysis shows that Pareto-aware optimization retains intermediate candidates that would be discarded by deployment preference but can support later improvements, while Bayesian bootstrap screening filters out candidates whose gains are weakly supported across runs.
